02 · Fibre type

Load packages

pacman::p_load(here, limma, dplyr, tidyr, tibble, readr, ggplot2, writexl)
here::i_am("06_Composition/02_fibre_type/a_script/02_fibre_type.qmd")

Read proteins and reference

FibeRtypeR (Van der Stede et al. 2026, doi:10.1113/JP290082) reads each biopsy as a mix of a pure slow (type I) and a pure fast (type II) fibre profile. Its proteomics markers are the 77 slow and 68 fast proteins of its Table S1 (Shared and Proteome columns). As in the paper, the reference is sex-specific: each marker’s median log2 abundance in the slow and in the fast pre-training fibre pools of each sex (12 pools per sex and type) of Moesgaard et al. 2026 (doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77275-9, PRIDE PXD056664), the data FibeRtypeR’s proteomics reference was built from; references/fibertyper_reference.csv holds both. The bulk input is the limpa matrix rather than DIA-NN’s LFQ, because limpa’s complete matrix measures more markers in every sample.

stage <- here("06_Composition", "02_fibre_type")
proteins <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "proteins.rds"))
d <- readRDS(here("02_Differential_Expression", "01_Design", "c_data", "design.rds"))
reference <- read_csv(file.path(stage, "references", "fibertyper_reference.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE)
targets <- proteins$targets
stopifnot(identical(rownames(d$design), targets$sample_id))
count(reference, marker_type)
# A tibble: 2 × 2
  marker_type     n
  <chr>       <int>
1 fast           68
2 slow           77

Estimate the slow fraction

Markers are matched to the matrix by gene symbol, one row per symbol, and kept when both sexes’ references have them. Each sample is fitted against its own sex’s reference, and shifted so its median over the markers equals that reference’s, because limpa’s scale differs from the deposit’s. For two fractions that are non-negative and sum to one, the least-squares fit FibeRtypeR runs (DeconRNASeq, equivalently limSolve::lsei()) has a closed form: the projection of the sample onto the line from the fast to the slow profile, clipped to [0, 1].

stopifnot(identical(colnames(proteins$E), targets$sample_id))
genes <- proteins$genes$Genes
reference <- filter(reference, !is.na(slow_F + fast_F + slow_M + fast_M))
rows <- which(genes %in% reference$gene & !duplicated(genes))
bulk <- proteins$E[rows, ]
marker_profile <- reference[match(genes[rows], reference$gene), ]
slow_ref <- as.matrix(marker_profile[paste0("slow_", targets$sex)])
fast_ref <- as.matrix(marker_profile[paste0("fast_", targets$sex)])
bulk <- sweep(bulk, 2, apply(bulk, 2, median) - apply(rbind(slow_ref, fast_ref), 2, median))
direction <- slow_ref - fast_ref
slow <- colSums((bulk - fast_ref) * direction) / colSums(direction^2)
targets$slow <- pmin(pmax(slow, 0), 1)
count(marker_profile, marker_type)
# A tibble: 2 × 2
  marker_type     n
  <chr>       <int>
1 fast           48
2 slow           51
summary(targets$slow)
   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
 0.2193  0.3498  0.4239  0.4169  0.4741  0.6969

Checks without histology

No histology exists for these biopsies, so the level is unvalidated; the checks ask whether the ranking behaves like fibre type: a person’s two legs should agree, as should one leg’s two biopsies, most variation should sit between people, and women’s muscle is usually slower than men’s.

wide <- targets |>
  select(participant, leg, timepoint, slow) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(leg, timepoint), values_from = slow)
checks <- tibble(
  check = c(
    "left vs right leg at T1 (r)", "same leg, T1 vs T2 (r)",
    "variance between participants (R2)", "women minus men (points)"
  ),
  value = c(
    cor(wide$L_T1, wide$R_T1, use = "complete.obs"),
    cor(c(wide$L_T1, wide$R_T1), c(wide$L_T2, wide$R_T2), use = "complete.obs"),
    summary(lm(slow ~ participant, targets))$r.squared,
    100 * (mean(targets$slow[targets$sex == "F"]) - mean(targets$slow[targets$sex == "M"]))
  )
)
mutate(checks, value = round(value, 2))
# A tibble: 4 × 2
  check                              value
  <chr>                              <dbl>
1 left vs right leg at T1 (r)         0.69
2 same leg, T1 vs T2 (r)              0.77
3 variance between participants (R2)  0.77
4 women minus men (points)            4.23

Did training or arm shift fibre type?

The slow fraction goes through the stage 02 design (group, participant, blood index) and its five contrasts as a single outcome row, so the test is the plain least-squares t, as for MPE in 05_Mitochondria. Estimates are in percentage points.

fit <- contrasts.fit(lmFit(rbind(slow = 100 * targets$slow), d$design), d$contrasts)
slow_tests <- tibble(
  contrast = colnames(d$contrasts), points = fit$coefficients[1, ],
  se = fit$stdev.unscaled[1, ] * fit$sigma, df = fit$df.residual
) |>
  mutate(
    p = 2 * pt(-abs(points / se), df),
    conf.low = points - qt(0.975, df) * se, conf.high = points + qt(0.975, df) * se
  )
group_summary <- targets |>
  summarise(mean = 100 * mean(slow), sd = 100 * sd(slow), n = n(), .by = c(treatment, timepoint))
group_summary

3       BFR        T1 41.42951  9.682921 33
4       BFR        T2 42.83866 10.004587 32
mutate(slow_tests, across(where(is.double), function(x) signif(x, 3)))

Figure

Each leg’s slow fraction before and after training, one line per leg, by arm.

figure <- targets |>
  mutate(leg_id = paste(participant, leg)) |>
  ggplot(aes(timepoint, 100 * slow, group = leg_id)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = treatment), size = 1.4, show.legend = FALSE) +
  stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "line", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(BFR = "#D55E00", HLRT = "#0072B2")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Slow (type I) fibre fraction, %",
    title = "Fibre type before and after training") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9)
figure
pdf(file.path(stage, "b_reports", "02_fibre_type.pdf"), width = 8.27, height = 5)
print(figure)
invisible(dev.off())

Save results

write_xlsx(
  list(
    slow_fraction = select(targets, sample_id, participant, leg, treatment, timepoint, sex, slow),
    contrasts = slow_tests,
    group_summary = group_summary,
    checks = checks
  ),
  file.path(stage, "c_data", "02_fibre_type.xlsx")
)
